newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. team in Iraq to discuss outlet with Syria.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team in Iraq to discuss outlet with Syria.

text.p: United Nations experts are currently in Iraq holding talks with officials on opening a border point with Syria to help ease the flow of goods under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the U.N., a U.N. official in Baghdad said on Sunday.
"A team of special experts from the sanctions committee is currently in Iraq to discuss a possible option for the opening of a fourth border point...with Syria," the source told Reuters.

Iraq has asked the sanctions committe to allow it to use a Syrian-Iraqi border point to handle some of its purchases under the deal. Food, medicine and other humanitarian goods purchased by Baghdad under the oil deal are now reaching the country through Umm Qasr port in southern Iraq, Jordan and Turkey.

Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis hard-hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. official, who asked not to be named, said the team would visit a border point between the two countries to see if its facilities could cope with the arrival of goods.
Syrian officials have announced that Syria's Mediterranean ports were ready to handle Iraq's imports under the oil pact.
Iraq and Syria decided last month to reopen their borders for trade, closed since the beginning of the 1980s when ties were cut because Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq- Iran war.

Since then the two countries have been exchaning economic teams. Iraqi trade ministry said last month that it had signed with visiting Syrian traders several deals to supply wheat, beans, soap and detergents under the oil deal.
